newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Monday were $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by light packer demand which was again linked to unprofitable operating margins, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants, dealers and packer buyers there said.

Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $56.00 to $56.50 at plants, sources there said. Indiana hogs also sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $53.50 to $54.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants.
Ohio hog prices slipped $0.50 to top prices of $53.00 to $54.00 in the country and $55.00 to $56.00 at plants.
Hog movement in the Midwest was relatively light despite rain over the weekend in some areas which stalled planting, dealers said.
"There's not that many hogs moving, guys are saying they don't want to sell at these prices," a central Iowa source said.
Some plants, including those operated by ConAgra Inc unit Swift and Co will be operating at reduced hours for the third consecutive week.
